note: Europe in 1871: the German Empire is proclaimed, Italy has just taken Rome, Austria-Hungary is a dual monarchy, France is a republic, and the Balkans, Bosnia and Cyprus are still Ottoman.

properties.info: The Third Republic was proclaimed in September 1870 after Napoleon III fell at Sedan; France lost Alsace and part of Lorraine and put down the Paris Commune in 1871.
Italy was almost unified: Venetia was gained in 1866 and Rome was taken from the Pope in 1870 (capital from 1871); Trento and Trieste were still Austrian.
Morocco was an independent sultanate under Muhammad IV (1859-73), under growing European pressure.
Russia under Alexander II had freed the serfs in 1861 and was expanding in Central Asia and the Caucasus; Poland, the Baltic provinces and Finland were under the tsar.
Persia was ruled by Naser al-Din Shah of the Qajar dynasty, balancing between Russia and Britain.
After the Revolution of 1868 ousted Isabella II, Spain was ruled by Amadeo of Savoy (1870-73), followed by the First Republic.
Portugal under Luís I (1861-89) was a constitutional monarchy with African colonies.
France had ruled Algeria since 1830; Tunisia was still a nominally Ottoman beylik until the protectorate of 1881.

The Ottoman Empire still held the whole Balkans from Bosnia and Bulgaria to Thessaly and Macedonia, plus Anatolia, the Levant, Iraq, the Hejaz, Cyprus and Libya; Serbia and Romania were autonomous vassals.
The Kingdom of the Netherlands under William III (1849-90).
Luxembourg was a neutral grand duchy (since 1867) in personal union with the Netherlands.
The German Empire was proclaimed at Versailles on 18 January 1871 under Wilhelm I of Prussia, uniting the North German Confederation with the southern states; Alsace was annexed from France.
Sweden and Norway were in a personal union under Charles XV (d. 1872, succeeded by Oscar II); Norway kept its own constitution and parliament.
Finland was a grand duchy under the Russian tsar since 1809, with its own diet.
The Dual Monarchy of Austria and Hungary was created by the Compromise of 1867 under Franz Joseph I; Bosnia was still Ottoman.
Greece received the Ionian Islands from Britain in 1864; Thessaly, Epirus, Macedonia and Crete were still Ottoman.
Montenegro was a small mountain principality around Cetinje under Nicholas I; it was recognised as independent only in 1878, when it roughly doubled in size.
Belgium became independent in 1830; Leopold II reigned from 1865.
Denmark lost Schleswig-Holstein to Prussia and Austria in 1864 but kept Iceland and the Faroe Islands.
The United Kingdom was the leading industrial and naval power, with Gladstone as prime minister; Queen Victoria reigned until 1901.

properties.label: Ottoman Empire
properties.info: Bulgaria was still a set of Ottoman provinces; the autonomous principality came only in 1878.
Bosnia and Herzegovina were Ottoman until Austria-Hungary occupied them in 1878.
Cyprus was Ottoman until Britain took over its administration in 1878.
Thessaly was Ottoman until it was ceded to Greece in 1881.
Egypt was a semi-autonomous Ottoman khedivate; Isma’il opened the Suez Canal in 1869 and ran up huge debts.
Serbia was an autonomous principality under Ottoman suzerainty; it gained independence and the Niš region only in 1878, and became a kingdom in 1882.
Wallachia and Moldavia united in 1859 and Carol I of Hohenzollern became prince in 1866; Romania was still under Ottoman suzerainty and Dobruja was Ottoman.
These districts were Ottoman until Montenegro took them in 1878.
The Bay of Kotor belonged to the Austrian Kingdom of Dalmatia.

properties.label: Tunis
properties.info: Tunisia was a nominally Ottoman beylik, effectively autonomous and deep in debt; France made it a protectorate in 1881.
These districts (including the Sanjak of Novi Pazar) were Ottoman until Serbia took them in 1878 (Novi Pazar until 1912).
Dobruja was Ottoman until it passed to Romania in 1878.
